analysis.title: Midday Market Intelligence: keep it moving
key_insights: US stocks traded higher on Wednesday Oct 28, 2026 after the FOMC held rates steady, as expected, with MSFT and GOOGL earnings due after the close.
GS reads FOMC participant comments since September as pointing to a compromise of raising the funds rate every other meeting, which the October hold supports. GS expects a second hike in December.
GEV beat expectations and raised its full-year guide to >130GW (vs 125GW prior and 100GW at the start of the year). Power orders were $29bn, +96% organic (Joe Ritchie).
VRT, FLEX, TEL and APH all reported strong results, pointing to demand for connectors, cables, electrical components and other hardware for data centers (Mark Delaney).
EVR reported pre-tax income 70% above consensus, with material beats in Advisory and ECM and disciplined costs (James Yaro).
AEP beat 3Q26 EPS expectations and introduced a $100bn 2027-2031 capital plan, up from the prior $78bn 2026-2030 plan (Carly Davenport).
DINO beat earnings expectations on stronger refining results, tight transportation fuel supply, elevated crack spreads and EPA small refinery RIN waivers (Neil Mehta).
CSGP was among the worst S&P 500 performers on the day despite strong revenue growth, on lower transaction volumes at Domain and softer subscription revenue at Apartments.com (George Tong).
LII missed on 3Q26 segment EBIT, driven by worse than expected sales and margins in Resi HVAC (Joe Ritchie).

On GOOGL, Eric Sheridan sees two debates: the integrated tech stack, with Google Cloud commentary as evidence, and Search revenue growth, the absence of a formal consumer agent launch, and positioning if consumer behavior moves to agentic interfaces.

On MSFT, Gabriela Borges sees an upside case of Azure growth of 46-47% cc (vs 44-45% cc guidance) and 2QFY guidance of about 46-47% cc. She also looks for broadening monetization through Copilot, agents, consumption workloads and E7, and M365 Commercial Cloud growth of about 17-18% cc (vs 17% guidance).

Chart of the Day (Megan Peters, Joseph Briggs): GS estimates AI demand adds 0.2-0.3pp to core inflation in non-US developed markets through 1Q27, fading sharply in sequential terms in most DMs in 2H27 as AI electronic input price pressure diminishes.
Calendar: 3Q PCE, 3Q GDP and weekly jobless claims on Thursday. MSFT, GOOGL and NOW report tonight. Many large caps report before the open Thursday, including LLY, MRK, CAT, MA and LIN.
